title: Jennifer Lawrence Says ‘I Can’t Do a Lot’ of Botox Because ‘I Need to Have Movement in My Face’ as an Actor, So ‘I Get Baby Botox’
description: Jennifer Lawrence opened up to Vogue about her relationship to cosmetic procedures and said she resists going overboard when it comes to botox becau
body:
Jennifer Lawrence opened up to Vogue about her relationship to cosmetic procedures and said she resists going overboard when it comes to botox because she is a working actor and facial movement is of the upmost important. The Oscar winner’s comment was published just a few weeks after Olivia Wilde put the industry on blast, telling Vogue that “it’s not easy” to find actresses to cast in movies because many of them can no longer move their faces.
	

	“I can’t really get very much done,” Lawrence told Vogue. “I need to have movement in my face — I get baby Botox, but I can’t do a lot. If my skin is going to be a little saggier than I would like, at least it looks dewy and pretty.” 


	Regarding the procedures she is hesitant to try, Lawrence said: “Oh, I’m really nervous about these fat transfers. I support other people doing them because I want to continue to watch and see what happens, but I don’t know about that. I mean, I would love to have a buccal fat removal. I can’t because everybody would know, but just know that I want that.”

	“I do like the radiofrequency because I have huge cheeks and so I feel like exercising them as much as possible,” she added.

	Olivia Wilde appeared on an episode of “The Run-Through with Vogue” during her summer press tour for “The Invite” when she noted: “As a director, I now am constantly searching for actresses who can still move their faces, and it’s not easy… I am a product of the same machine. I am under the same pressures. I get it.” 

	“There’s something so medieval about a lot of these things,” she added at the time. “I’ve had the thing of people being like, ‘She looks old and dead and awful.’ And you’re like, ‘Fuck! How do you win? It’s impossible.'”
	

	Lawrence was a fixture on last year’s awards circuit as the star of “Die My Love,” which premiered at Cannes and earned her a Golden Globe nomination for best actress in a motion picture drama. She’s expected to appear as her “Hunger Games” character Katniss Everdeen in a small role in this November’s prequel movie “Sunrise on the Reaping.” Lawrence’s next big headlining role is opposite Leonardo DiCaprio’s in Martin Scorsese’s “What Happens at Night.” The film is expected to arrive next year.

schema.headline: Jennifer Lawrence Says ‘I Can’t Do a Lot’ of Botox Because ‘I Need to Have Movement in My Face’ as an Actor, So ‘I Get Baby Botox’

title: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Announcer Jim Thornton Fired by Sony
description: “Wheel of Fortune” announcer Jim Thornton has been fired from the game show, producer Sony Pictures TV confirmed. “Following a thorough investigatio
body:
“Wheel of Fortune” announcer Jim Thornton has been fired from the game show, producer Sony Pictures TV confirmed. “Following a thorough investigation, Jim Thornton’s employment with ‘Wheel of Fortune’ has been terminated, effective immediately,” the studio said in a statement.

	According to insiders, Thornton won’t be heard on the show when it returns for a new season on September 14, as an interim announcer has revoiced all of Thornton’s parts on the shows. No permanent replacement has been announced.
	

	Thornton’s firing came just hours after TMZ posted photos of what were allegedly him on an American Airlines plane with his laptop opened on “disturbing chat room” that appeared to be “images and texts that made it appear it was a chat room for pedophiles.” The up-close photos of the laptop’s screen showed lewd conversations about minors.


	The alleged incident took place in May, when according to TMZ, a passenger informed a flight attendant about the chat screen on Thornton’s laptop. Authorities were waiting to question Thornton when his flight landed at LAX, and after they spoke to the Thornton he was given permission to leave.

	Neither Thornton nor his lawyer have publicly addressed the allegations; an attorney who said they represented the announcer, Allison Hart, told TMZ that Thornton had “become active in suicide-prevention advocacy since losing a close family member to suicide two years ago and he has spent time visiting chat rooms offering support to individuals suffering from suicidal ideation.”

	On Tuesday, Sony Pictures TV said that “we have recently been made aware of allegations concerning Jim Thornton. He has been suspended from ‘Wheel of Fortune’ and we are recasting while we conduct a thorough investigation.” 
	

	The announcer joined “Wheel” in 2010 after the death of the show’s previous announcer, Charlie O’Donnell, and has also worked as a substitute announcer on “The Price Is Right.” He’s also been the voice of “Celebrity Wheel of Fortune” on ABC.

	Thornton’s other credits include “Celebrity Deathmatch,” where he voiced Johnny Gomez, and as an announcer on “The Cleveland Show” and “Tim & Eric Awesome Show, Great Job!” He’s also been heard on several video games and appeared as a commercial narrator in the 2001 animated film “Monsters, Inc.” He also voiced the 2011 Oscar-nominated short animated film “Let’s Pollute.”

	Thornton has been a local media presence in Los Angeles for decades, having previously worked as an afternoon anchor on KNX 1070 Newsradio, which he first joined in 1985 as a traffic reporter with Metro Traffic. He also provided traffic reports on KCBS-TV.

	His other broadcast credits include Westwood One Radio Networks, and he was the voice of L.A.’s KCOP-TV for four years. He has received an Edward R. Murrow award, Golden Mike awards and an Emmy.

schema.headline: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Announcer Jim Thornton Fired by Sony

title: 17 Best Movies New to Streaming in September: ‘Toy Story 5,’ ‘Backrooms,’ ’Scary Movie 6,’ ’The Mandalorian and Grogu’
description:
Sep 4, 2026 2:20pm PT	
	

	
		17 Best Movies New to Streaming in September: ‘Toy Story 5,’ ‘Backrooms,’ ’Scary Movie 6,’ ’The Mandal
body:
Sep 4, 2026 2:20pm PT	
	

	
		17 Best Movies New to Streaming in September: ‘Toy Story 5,’ ‘Backrooms,’ ’Scary Movie 6,’ ’The Mandalorian and Grogu’
	
	
			


			
			
	

									Everett Collection 
	

		
	
				

	Labor Day Weekend brings to a close the summer movie season, which became one of the biggest on record thanks to the mega-blockbusters “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” But the season is just getting started on streaming platforms as some of the summer’s buzziest titles make their streaming debuts to kick off the fall movie corridor. 

	“Toy Story 5” is the third highest-grossing movie of the year with $1.13 billion and should prove to be a streaming mega-hit when it arrives on Disney+ near the end of the month. Expect the whole “Toy Story” animated franchise to get a streaming lift as a result. A24’s horror hit “Backrooms,” which became the studio’s highest-grossing title in history this summer, should also prove a streaming hit when it lands on HBO Max. Meanwhile, the “Star Wars” misfire “The Mandalorian and Grogu” hopes to rebound on Disney+ after stumbling in theaters. The movie is now available to stream, as is Paramount’s “Scary Movie 6.”

	Check out a full rundown below of the biggest new titles to streaming in September.


			
			
	Toy Story 5 (Sept. 23 on Disney+)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Walt Disney Co./Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Disney and Pixar’s animated blockbuster “Toy Story 5” arrives on Disney+ this month after earning $1.13 billion and counting at the summer box office, which makes it the third highest-grossing movie of 2026 so far (trailing “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey”). The sequel was also named one of Variety’s best movies of the year so far: “It escalates in delight (the climactic wedding ceremony must be seen to be believed), but it also has moments that hit you like a gut punch. The message is: Slow down, be real and play. The fun you take is equal to the fun you make.”
		
			
			
	Backrooms (Sept. 25 on HBO Max)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Kane Parsons’ horror smash “Backrooms” arrives on HBO Max this month after becoming A24’s highest-grossing movie of all time with $394 million at the worldwide box office. “As an atmospheric freakout, ‘Backrooms’ is extraordinarily effective,” Variety‘s chief film critic Owen Gleiberman wrote in his positive review, noting that Chiwetel Ejiofor was “the perfect presence to have at the center.” He also compared Parsons’ fixation for mood and “cosmic sound design” to the late David Lynch.
		
			
			
	The Mandalorian and Grogu (Disney+)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Walt Disney Co./Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	“The Mandalorian and Grogu” suffered at the summer box office with an $81 million domestic debut, an underwhelming start for a “Star Wars” movie. The film went on to earn $345 million worldwide, far below the billion-dollar grosses of the previous “Star Wars” film releases “The Rise of Skywalker” and “The Last Jedi.” But can “The Mandalorian and Grogu” rebound on streaming? Directed by Jon Favreau, the movie follows bounty hunter Din Djarin (Pedro Pascal) and his apprentice, Grogu, as they’re recruited by officer Colonel Ward (Sigourney Weaver) to aid the New Republic. The unlikely duo must rescue the heir to Jabba the Hutt, Rotta the Hutt (voiced by “The Bear’s” Jeremy Allen White), in order to track down an Imperial leader.
		
			
			
	Scary Movie (Paramount+) 
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Paramount/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	“Scary Movie,” also known as “Scary Movie 6,” is now streaming on Paramount+ after delighting the box office with a strong $231 million worldwide. An extended cut of the movie is also now streaming on the same platform. Returning cast members include Marlon Wayans (Shorty Meeks), Shawn Wayans (Ray), Anna Faris (Cindy Campbell) and Regina Hall (Brenda Meeks). Faris and Hall reprised their roles after neither appeared in “Scary Movie 5.”
		
			
			
	Supergirl (Sept. 10 on HBO Max)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	“Supergirl” soars to streaming on HBO Max on Sept. 10. There will also be an American Sign Language (ASL) version of “Supergirl” available to stream performed by Catalene Sacchetti (“Songs in Sign Language”) and directed by Jonaz McMillan (“The Pitt with ASL” Season One). Directed by Craig Gillespie and written by Ana Nogueira, the adaptation is based on the DC comic series “Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow” by Tom King. In the comic, Supergirl and a young alien girl named Ruthye travel across the galaxy to hunt down Krem of the Yellow Hill after he murders Ruthye’s father.
		
			
			
	Why Did I Get Married Again? (Sept. 9 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Per Netflix: “In Tyler Perry’s ‘Why Did I Get Married Again?’, the couples reunite in celebration as Marcus and Angela’s daughter prepares to tie the knot. After being apart for quite some time, they learn quickly that as much as things change, they stay the same. Realizing their children have grown up to be so much like them, they must reflect on the examples they’ve set and ask themselves that age-old question, why did they get married… again?” The cast includes Tyler Perry, Taraji P. Henson, Jill Scott, Richard T. Jones, Tasha Smith, Michael Jai White, Sharon Leal and more.
		
			
			
	Unabomber (Sept. 25 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	“Room” breakout Jacob Tremblay is all grown up in Netflix’s “Unabomber,” where he stars in the title role. The movie tracks Ted Kaczynski’s transformation from 16-year-old Harvard prodigy into the infamous Unabomber. Per Netflix: “Subjected to controversial psychological experiments by Professor Henry Murray (Russell Crowe), Kaczynski’s troubled past resurfaces decades later when his manhunt, led by FBI agent Joanne Miller (Shailene Woodley), brings to light the chilling consequences of ambition and isolation.”
		
			
			
	Call My Agent! The Movie (Sept. 10 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Camille Cottin and the rest of the “Call My Agent!” gang return for the feature film follow-up. Per Netflix: “Five years after the agency closed its doors, Andréa is finally ready to direct her first feature film. When her lead actor quits and she falls out with her producer, she joins forces with Noémie—now a successful reality TV producer—believing she can easily manipulate her. But as she faces a complete recasting, on-set disasters, and a legal battle threatening the custody of her daughter, everything begins to unravel.”
		
			
			
	The Love Hypothesis (Sept. 23 on Prime Video)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Amazon/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	 Lili Reinhart and Tom Bateman hope to deliver a romance knockout for Amazon Prime Video with the launch of “The Love Hypothesis,” based on the best-selling novel by Ali Hazelwood. Per the synopsis: “Olive (Reinhart), a brilliant Ph.D. candidate focused on her future in academia, realizes her best friend Ahn (Rachel Marsh) has fallen for her crush Jeremy (Nicholas Duvernay), so Olive impulsively kisses intimidating professor Adam Carlsen (Tom Bateman) to prove she’s moved on. What begins as a desperate act of friendship spirals into a fake relationship with rules, boundaries, and a mutually beneficial agreement.”
		
			
			
	Stop That Train (Sept. 20 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Directed by Adam Shankman, “Stop That Train!” stars RuPaul as President Gagwell and “Drag Race” alumni Ginger Minj and Jujubee as best friends who work on the glitzy Glamazonian Express train. When a catastrophic “Stormaganza” threatens to derail the high-speed locomotive and crash it into Los Angeles, the duo in coach must join forces with the snobby first class attendants (Raven-Symone, Brooke Lynn Hytes, Marcia Marcia Marcia) to save the day. Matt Rogers, Sarah Michelle Gellar, Rachel Bloom, Lisa Rinna and Nicole Richie also star in the film.
		
			
			
	The Runner (Sept. 2 on Prime Video)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Amazon/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Gal Gadot is top billed in Prime Video’s real-time action thriller “The Runner.” Per the streamer: “Maia Marten (Gal Gadot) has built her life on being one step ahead — a sharp, resourceful, high-powered lawyer at the top of London’s legal world.  During her routine morning run, a single phone call shatters her world: her son has been taken. The instructions to get him back are simple and merciless — keep moving, follow every command, and tell no one. Stop, and he dies. Forced to sprint through the city and obey a series of sinister commands, Maia must confront an impossible question: how far will she go to bring her son home?”
		
			
			
	Fuze (Sept. 4 on HBO Max)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Roadside Attractions/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	A ticking bomb in the heart of London sets the stage for “Fuze,” a taut British crime thriller from director David Mackenzie. Written by Ben Hopkins, the feature stars Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Theo James, Gugu Mbatha-Raw and Sam Worthington. As the military and police scramble to evacuate the city when a World War II bomb is unearthed at a bustling construction site, chaos unfolds across London’s streets.
		
			
			
	100 Nights of Hero (Sept. 18 on Hulu)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©IFC Films/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	Julia Jackman wrote and directed this adaptation of Isabel Greenberg’s bestselling graphic novel, “The One Hundred Nights of Hero.” Emma Corrin, Nicholas Galitzine, Maika Monroe, Amir El-Masry, Charli XCX, Richard E. Grant and Felicity Jones star. The movie follows a woman named Cherry (Monroe), whose neglectful husband departs after placing a secret wager to test her fidelity. Along with her sharp-witted maid, Hero (Corrin), Cherry must fend off a dangerously seductive visitor: Manfred (Galitzine).
		
			
			
	The Plague (Sept. 25 on Hulu)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©IFC Films/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	“The Plague” is an unconventional horror tale about a young boy named Ben (Everett Blunck), who is new to the social structure of an all-boys water polo camp. Other children, under the direction of their cruel peer Jake (Kayo Martin) and with very little adult supervision, alienate shy young Eli (Kenny Rasmussen) by saying he has the titular disease. Things get uncomfortable from there. Joel Edgerton co-stars.
		
			
			
	The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist (Sept. 15 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Focus Features/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	“The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist” explores the intersection of AI development and humanity.  The Focus Features release follows a father-to-be as he tries to figure out what is happening with all this AI insanity, aka the most powerful technology humanity has ever created, and what’s at stake if we get it wrong  Per Variety: “Daniel Roher, the director of ‘Navalny,’ has made a heady documentary that explores the future of artificial intelligence with fearlessly open eyes.”
		
			
			
	Best of the Best (Sept. 18 on Netflix)
			
										
					Image Credit: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				
	“Never Have I Ever” star Maitreyi Ramakrishnan returns to Netflix with the high-energy comedy “Best of the Best.” Per the streamer: “Two childhood best friends, Maya and Anjali, join UCLA’s competitive Bollywood-fusion dance team, only to discover that the road to winning the U.S. Championship is far more raucous and cutthroat than they ever imagined.”
		
			
			
	The Widower: ‘Til Death Do Us Part (Sept. 30 on Netflix)
			
								
				
	Documentary filmmaker Chris Smith keeps his Netflix collaboration going strong after ” Jim & Andy: The Great Beyond” (2017), “Fyre” (2019), “Sr.” (2022), and “Wham!” (2023) with the true crime doc “The Widower: ‘Til Death Do Us Part.” Per the streamer: “In this documentary, a journalist and a detective uncover the truth about a killer whose charm masked a trail of failed marriages and suspicious deaths.”

title: Rob Rausch and Maura Higgins to Host Survival Competition Show for Peacock ‘Get Me Out of Here’
description:
Rob Rausch and Maura Higgins are returning to reality TV — this time as hosts.

	The “Traitors” and “Love Island” alums will lead a new competition
body:
Rob Rausch and Maura Higgins are returning to reality TV — this time as hosts.

	The “Traitors” and “Love Island” alums will lead a new competition series with the working title “Get Me Out of Here,” set to air on Peacock sometime in 2027.

	From ITV America, the series flings celebrities into a “dense and unforgiving jungle” with a non-famous friend or family member. In the ultimate test of friendship, the duos must survive a “series of physical and psychological challenges” to avoid elimination. In the wild, the celebs are stripped of every luxury and the perks of being famous.
	

	The last remaining team will win a $100,000 grand prize.


	Per the logline, “Relying on each other like never before, teams must navigate everything the jungle throws their way as their grit, stamina and resilience are pushed to the limit. With their bonds under pressure, the jungle will reveal which celebs can adapt to life without the VIP treatment, and which BFFs can handle being stuck in the jungle with a star.”

	“Get Me Out of Here” is produced by ITV America. David George, David Eilenberg and Jordana Hochman are executive producers. The series is based on the international format “I’m a Celebrity…Get Me Out of Here!,” created by Lifted Entertainment and distributed by ITV Studios.

	Rausch is the sole winner of “The Traitors” Season 4 who became a breakout star on “Love Island USA.” Higgins was a finalist on the fifth season of the British “Love Island” and was a contestant on “Dancing With the Stars” among other reality shows.

schema.headline: Rob Rausch and Maura Higgins to Host Survival Competition Show for Peacock ‘Get Me Out of Here’

title: How John Malkovich’s 30-Year Oscar Drought Could Finally End With ‘Wild Horse Nine’
description:
John Malkovich could finally have an Oscar secret weapon, and his name is Martin McDonagh.

	“Wild Horse Nine,” the black comedy that bowed in compe
body:
John Malkovich could finally have an Oscar secret weapon, and his name is Martin McDonagh.

	“Wild Horse Nine,” the black comedy that bowed in competition at the Venice Film Festival — where it drew a 13-minute standing ovation — before turning up as Telluride’s surprise patron screening on Friday afternoon, drops a pair of CIA operatives onto Easter Island in the tense days before the 1973 Chilean coup, then lets the absurdity metastasize from there.
	

	The ensemble is deep and soars — Steve Buscemi, Tom Waits, Parker Posey, Chilean breakout star Mariana Di Girolamo — but the film rests on its firm two-hander: Sam Rockwell and, in the performance generating the loudest awards buzz, Malkovich.


	A McDonagh movie arrives with automatic awards gravity, and he’s earned it. “Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri” and “The Banshees of Inisherin” both turned festival launches into major Oscar players — the former landing seven nominations, the latter nine — and both proved his unusual ability to make the Academy take a particular kind of movie seriously: profane, melancholy and frequently very funny, with enough emotional heft to shrug off the label of “comedy.”



	

					Steve Buscemi and Sam Rockwell in “Wild Horse Nine” 
									Searchlight Pictures
	



	Searchlight Pictures, for its part, knows the route from the Lido to the Dolby — one of the last two ceremonies the Oscars will stage there before the show decamps to downtown L.A. and YouTube in 2029 — and has a long track record of positioning filmmaker-driven works as contenders without sanding down the eccentricities.
	

	But the most intriguing Oscar question around “Wild Horse Nine” may not be best picture-related at all. It’s simpler: Is it finally Malkovich time?

	He has two Oscar nominations, both in supporting actor — for “Places in the Heart” in 1984 and “In the Line of Fire” in 1993 — and he lost both. Then, essentially, the conversation stopped. “Dangerous Liaisons” fell in between; “Being John Malkovich” and “Burn After Reading” came after. None of it brought him back to the Academy’s acting conversation.

	For more than three decades he has made movies, television and theater, delivering some of the most indelible performances of his generation without once returning to the Academy’s radar. That absence is exactly what makes “Wild Horse Nine” such a fascinating vehicle for a comeback. McDonagh’s films are populated by characters who are funny because they’re wounded, dangerous because they’re ridiculous and tragic because they can’t quite grasp what they want.

	Malkovich, dropped into that tonal universe, has an almost unfair advantage. His signature gifts — menace at a whisper, deadpan absurdity, theatrical precision, and the knack for making even the strangest line land like an anvil. The role could become a classic overdue narrative without asking voters to engage in revisionist history. He has already been there. He just hasn’t been back since the Reagan and Clinton administrations.

	The Academy has always had an appetite for career reassessments, especially when an established actor lands in the right filmmaker’s hands — see Gary Oldman in “Darkest Hour.” But Malkovich isn’t walking in needing voters to discover him. He needs them to remember what made him singular in the first place, and McDonagh may be the filmmaker best positioned to jog that memory.

	“Wild Horse Nine” has to prove the formula still works in a field that is destined to be crowded. A festival pedigree no longer guarantees a best picture nomination; Venice and Telluride will mint dozens of contenders, and the Academy’s appetite for difficult comedies runs notoriously hot and cold. McDonagh has earned the benefit of the doubt, but even his brand has to be reactivated. So the first question isn’t whether “Wild Horse Nine” can be nominated for best picture. It’s whether the film can become a top-tier contender. I think it can.
	

	Malkovich is the obvious story for Searchlight, but hardly the only one. Rockwell could steamroll into supporting actor — where sources say he’ll campaign — and, much as his “Three Billboards” run helped pull co-star Woody Harrelson into the category alongside him, his momentum here could lift the veteran and criminally never-nominated Buscemi. Di Girolamo, the Chilean star Pablo Larraín introduced to the world in “Ema,” could break through with American voters and enter the supporting actress conversation.



	

					Mariana di Girolamo and John Malkovich in “Wild Horse Nine” 
									Searchlight Pictures
	



	Waits and Posey make the ensemble itself part of the film’s awards identity — an asset at the Screen Actors Guild Awards, where a group campaign can build momentum even when any single performance is fighting for oxygen. The Oscar math is trickier. 

	And then there’s the backdrop. “Wild Horse Nine” unfolds around the 1973 Chilean coup — one of the most consequential and contested episodes of the Cold War — and dropping CIA operatives into a black comedy set there hands the film an unavoidable political charge. How will voters read it in 2026? As history, as satire, as a commentary on American power or some volatile mix of all three?

	The Academy has never been allergic to politically charged movies, but tone decides everything. A film that uses history to illuminate the present can feel urgent; one that seems to force present-day politics onto a historical story risks becoming a referendum on the moment rather than the movie.

	For all the best picture, screenplay and ensemble possibilities, Malkovich remains the clearest story to embrace. There’s something inherently cinematic about a great actor returning to the Oscar race after such a long absence.

	But the Oscars aren’t only about legacy. They’re about timing — and timing may finally be on his side. The Academy managed to forget Malkovich for the better part of 30 years. 

	Leave it to McDonagh to make that impossible again.

schema.headline: How John Malkovich’s 30-Year Oscar Drought Could Finally End With ‘Wild Horse Nine’

title: ‘Spider-Noir’ Canceled by Prime Video After One Season
description: It was a dark and stormy night for “Spider-Noir.” The Prime Video/MGM+ series, starring Nicolas Cage in his first-ever regular TV role, has been can
body:
It was a dark and stormy night for “Spider-Noir.” The Prime Video/MGM+ series, starring Nicolas Cage in his first-ever regular TV role, has been canceled after eight episodes and won’t return for a Season 2.

	The news comes even as “Spider-Noir” heads into the first weekend of Emmy ceremonies with 11 nominations — the most of any Prime Video program this year. The series also has a solid 92% rating on Rotten Tomatoes (and a 90% “popcornmeter” vote among fans).
	

	“Spider-Noir” was the first Marvel-related series to premiere out of Amazon’s pact with Sony Pictures TV to develop characters and stories from the “Sony Pictures Universe of Marvel Characters.” 


	Sony notes that its oversight includes more than 900 Marvel characters associated with the Spider-Man franchise. The second series to come out of that partnership is already in development and is expected to be announced soon.

	“Spider-Noir” was based on the Marvel Comics character Spider-Man Noir, and was adapted for television by Oren Uziel. The series takes place during the Great Depression and stars Cage as Ben Reilly, “a seasoned, down-on-his-luck private investigator in 1930s New York, who is forced to grapple with his past life following a deeply personal tragedy, as the city’s one and only superhero.”

	Lamorne Morris (“New Girl”), Li Jun Li (“Sinners”), Karen Rodriguez (“The Hunting Wives”), Abraham Popoola (“Atlas”), Jack Huston (“Boardwalk Empire”), and Brendan Gleeson (“The Banshees of Inisherin”) also star. 

	Uziel (“The Lost City”) and Steve Lightfoot (“Marvel’s The Punisher”) are showrunners and executive producers. Phil Lord and Christopher Miller executive produce for Lord Miller, along with Aditya Sood and Dan Shear. Amy Pascal is executive producer via Pascal Pictures. Cage and Pavlina Hatoupis are also executive producers. Harry Bradbeer (“Fleabag”) directed and executive produced the first two episodes. 
	

	“Spider-Noir” originally premiered on the linear MGM+ channel on May 25, and then started streaming on Prime Video the next day — with options to watch the show in either color or black & white. According to Nielsen’s streaming content ratings, the series earned 2.6 billion viewing minutes in its first six weeks.

	Among the show’s 11 Emmy nominations: Outstanding Production Design For A Narrative Period Or Fantasy Program (One Hour Or More), Outstanding Title Design, Outstanding Sound Mixing For A Comedy Or Drama Series (One Hour), Outstanding Sound Editing For A Comedy Or Drama Series (One Hour), Outstanding Cinematography For A Series (One Hour), Outstanding Stunt Performance, Outstanding Music Composition For A Series (Original Dramatic Score), Outstanding Special Visual Effects In A Single Episode, Outstanding Stunt Coordination For Comedy Programming, Outstanding Prosthetic Makeup, and Outstanding Original Music And Lyrics.

	As for Amazon’s deal to develop multiple live-action shows based on the Marvel characters controlled by Sony, the first project originally greenlit was “Silk: Spider Society,” with Angela Kang as showrunner, but that show was later scrapped. That meant “Spider-Noir” instead was the first release under the arrangement.

	 In film, Sony has released multiple Spider-Man live-action films over the years and currently works with Marvel Studios on the franchise starring Tom Holland via Columbia Pictures. The studio is currently riding high with “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which just hit $900 million at the box office domestically, and more than $2.3 billion globally.

schema.headline: ‘Spider-Noir’ Canceled by Prime Video After One Season

body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Formula 1 heads to one of its most storied tracks this weekend, as the Italian Grand Prix takes over the Autodromo Nazionale Monza.

	The 2026 Italian Grand Prix takes place Sunday, Sept. 6, with the race starting at 9 a.m. ET/6 a.m. PT. Apple TV’s race-day coverage begins at 7:50 a.m. ET. Practice sessions began Friday, Sept. 4, while the final practice and qualifying take place Saturday.


	The easiest way to watch the Monza Grand Prix in the U.S. is with an Apple TV subscription, which costs $14.99 per month after a seven-day free trial for new subscribers. 


	The 2026 campaign marks Formula 1’s first season under its new U.S. broadcasting agreement with Apple. The companies announced a five-year partnership last October making Apple TV the exclusive American home of F1 beginning this season, replacing ESPN, which had carried the sport in the U.S. since 2018.

	There should be plenty worth tuning in for at Monza. Italian driver Kimi Antonelli enters Round 13 atop the drivers’ standings with 242 points, holding a 59-point advantage over Mercedes teammate George Russell. Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton is tied with Russell at 183 points, followed by McLaren’s Lando Norris at 159 and Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc at 155. Mercedes also leads the constructors’ championship with 425 points, ahead of Ferrari at 338 and McLaren at 263.

A three-day Sling Orange pass costs $9.99, while a seven-day pass costs $14.99, with both providing access to ESPN and ESPN2 without requiring a full monthly subscription.

	The tournament arrives as ESPN begins a new chapter in its long-running relationship with the USTA. A 12-year media-rights agreement that went into effect this year keeps the U.S. Open on ESPN through 2037 and expands the company’s streaming coverage beginning with the 2026 tournament. ESPN has held exclusive U.S. rights to the event since 2015.


	This year, that expansion includes a new “RedZone at the US Open” stream, available to ESPN Unlimited subscribers through Friday, Sept. 4. Modeled after the familiar whip-around format, the seven-hour daily feed jumps among all 16 courts to catch pivotal games, match points and other live action.

title: ‘The Basics of Philosophy’ Review: Paul Schrader Wrestles with Sin and Spinoza in His Latest Tortured-Man Drama
description: Another man, another room, another vile past deed in need of expiation. On the one hand you could accuse writer-director Paul Schrader of retreading
body:
Another man, another room, another vile past deed in need of expiation. On the one hand you could accuse writer-director Paul Schrader of retreading old ground with his latest unadorned exploration of guilt, transgression and the intellectual work that a sinner must do in order to seek redemption for his sins. On the other hand, you cannot ever accuse Paul Schrader of taking the easy way out when there is available to him a difficult way to get deeper in.
	

	If Schrader here is embracing familiar themes, there is nothing comfortable about this embrace, given that those themes, present in the majority of his recent output, can be reduced to the same question, reformulated each time to a different, and differently heinous, model. In “The Card Counter,” he wondered if it is possible to once have been, but no longer be, a torturer. In “Master Gardener,” he pondered whether one could once have been, but no longer be, a Nazi. And with this new film, his endless preoccupations approach once again a kind of moral event-horizon of awfulness: Is it possible to once have been a pedophile?


	The opening of “The Basics of Philosophy” puts Jack Huston‘s Prof. John Jorrisen in front of a blackboard on which is written “The Basics of Philosophy,” as he talks to his students about his course, “The Basics of Philosophy,” while trying to elicit from them their own impressions of, well, the basics of philosophy. This bluntly presentational approach is either damningly clumsy, or daringly straightforward, depending on which side of the Schrader Dividing Line you fall. And wherever you have landed in the past, this film — what was it called again? — is unlikely to be the one that will shift you from one column to the other. 
	

	But for those who find (and in some cases may be slightly mystified as to why) that there is a nagging, needling value to Schrader’s ongoing project of tussling with grandiose dilemmas of transgression and deliverance, there is some new news here. For one thing, Schrader’s collaboration with ace DP Sean Price Williams lends bit more visual interest to the ascetic, bordering on bland, aesthetic he has established before. And for another, the seriousness of Schrader’s intentions, however uneven the outcome, are flattered by the somber mood established by Eli Kezsler’s restless, haunted score. 

	Still, an air of artificiality and sometimes theatricality does pervade his talky, often didactic scenes, which actually plays to the benefit of the performances — especially from Huston. He is impressive here because of the peculiar intensity of his gaze, the too-smoothly-controlled, cultured timbre of his voice, the general sense of something about him being just that bit off.

	John teaches at a small, leafy college by day, while by night working on a book about rationalist philosopher Spinoza and dating his beautiful colleague Becca (Sofia Boutella), a professor of psychology who has a son with whom John gets along well. John’s father Melvyn (Bill Pullman), a wealthy captain-of-industry-type whose relationship with his son has been under some unnamed strain for a long time, is in hospital, dying. At his funeral, John delivers a eulogy with a terseness he claims is in tribute to his father’s love of precision and economy of language. 

	But he stumbles over the plain words, when he spots Miguel Vasque (an excellent Daniel Zovatto) sitting in one of the pews. As relayed through flashbacks more suggestive than graphic and that employ the rather cheaply televisual trick of being rendered in high-contrast black and white to blast out the age lines on the actors’ faces, many years before, John had been giving piano lessons to 14-year-old Miguel (Trevor Dolden), the son of the family’s gardener. At one of those sessions, John sexually abused the boy, then immediately confessed as much to his father, who undertook, essentially, a lifetime of financial and emotional support for Miguel and his family in order to atone for — and also to cover up — his son’s crime.
	

	John seeks out a confrontation with Miguel, now a successful realtor. It seems like the story will plot a direct course as a perpetrator seeks forgiveness from his victim — even allowing for a frankly bizarre interlude where John strolls through a park chatting with an unconvincingly bewigged Spinoza (Karl Glusman), in perhaps this staggeringly serious drama’s only attempt at levity. But his past with Miguel – who is always a threatening and slightly sinister presence for John, but is also pretty much the only character who acts with decency and without deceit throughout — is only one aspect of an increasingly knotted-up narrative. The film soon takes on the strangely idiosyncratic shape of Schrader’s own intellectual obsessions, encompassing thwarted desire, suicide, self-delusion, self-examination and sins of the kind that permanently stain the soul, rather than proceeding with anything approaching psychological plausibility.

	John believes his rape of a child was a one-off, and he will never commit such an act again. John believes he is sorry. John believes he is not gay. John believes a lot of stuff, but behaves in ways that destabilize all those beliefs, that feel like Schrader arguing the points out in a way that compels even, and sometimes especially, when it fails to convince. 

	Like in the rest of his “Man in a Room” movies, with “The Basics of Philosophy,” Schrader betrays a self-aware intellectual and ethical vulnerability that is sincere and conflicted and hard to reconcile with the public Paul Schrader of the often indefensibly unreconstructed social media presence. But perhaps we should stop being surprised at these contradictions. As the ambivalent conclusion of “The Basics of Philosophy” suggests, yes, it is possible for a man to change. But as soon as you admit that truth, you must also admit the ever-present, looming possibility of him changing back.

title: Tetris Company Distances Itself From Trump White House’s ‘Build the Wall’ Game, Says ‘We Take Copyright Very Seriously’
description: The Tetris Company wants to be clear that it was not involved in the creation of the White House‘s “Build the Wall” game — an obvious copy of the fa
body:
The Tetris Company wants to be clear that it was not involved in the creation of the White House‘s “Build the Wall” game — an obvious copy of the famous block-dropping title — in which players must prevent zombie-like foreigners from crossing the “southern border” into the United States. The game company added, “We take copyright infringement very seriously.”

	On Thursday, the Trump White House launched the whitehouse.gov/arcade website with six games. One of those is called “Build the Wall,” which tells players to “Protect the border from the coming horde.”
	

	In a statement posted to social media Friday, the Tetris Company said: “At Tetris we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them. To our fans everywhere: we love you, we see you, and we’re grateful to have you in our community.”


	The company also said this: “P.S. The Tetris Company was not involved in the creation of ‘Build the Wall’. P.P.S. We take copyright infringement very seriously.”

	Here’s an image of the White House’s Tetris-like game, which includes the subtitle “ZOMBIE BORDER SIEGE.” The foreign invaders bounce off the wall a player has built and disintegrate, until the blocks have stacked above the upper bound and the game ends with the message “BORDER BREACHED.”



	

	



	Asked whether the Tetris Company was considering taking legal action with respect to the White House’s “Build the Wall” game, a company rep said it is “currently reviewing the matter.”

	“The Tetris Company was not involved in the creation of ‘Build the Wall’ and did not authorize or license the Tetris brand or intellectual property for the game,” the spokesperson said. “For more than 40 years, Tetris has brought people together across generations and cultures through play and joy. The objective of the game has always been to stack with purpose to clear as many lines as possible. We are currently reviewing the matter.”
	

	Variety has reached out to the White House for comment.

	Created in 1984, the Tetris brand “continues to be loved globally by people of all ages and all cultures,” the company says. Alexey Pajitnov, the Soviet programmer who is the game’s original creator, remains actively involved in the brand.

	Billions of Tetris games are played online every year, and over 520 million units have been sold worldwide. The Tetris brand’s global licensee network includes major video game publishers, including Nintendo and Sega, as well as many partners in electronics, toys and games, apparel, accessories, entertainment and other areas. 

	Tetris Holding LLC is the owner of Tetris rights worldwide, and the Tetris Company is its exclusive licensee.

body:
Trump's Ex-Labor Secretary
                          Allegedly Demanded Security Make It Rain on Stripper!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 4, 2026
                            9:22 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            President Donald Trump's former Secretary of Labor is a supporter of the working class ... because she apparently ordered a member of her security team to make it rain on a stripper.
      
    
            The Office of the Inspector General -- an office dedicated to government oversight -- released a report on Thursday detailing a series of sordid actions the office claims Lori Chavez-DeRemer committed while serving in Trump's Cabinet.
      
    
            The report specifically notes she went to a partially nude strip club in Oregon in April 2025 -- just a month after taking office -- where Secretary Chavez-DeRemer allegedly “took money from her purse, gave the money to the driver [a member of security detail], and directed him to give it to the performer.”
      

            OIG states this security detail member felt uncomfortable and went to his fellow agent, a man named Brian Sloan, who "instructed him to comply with Chavez-DeRemer’s requests."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            After the security guard did, Chavez-DeRemer allegedly pulled more money from her purse and asked the agent to drop the bills one by one on the performer. OIG says he hesitated again and went to Sloan, but was once again told to comply.
      
    
            Sloan factors in more heavily to the allegations against Chavez-DeRemer as well ... she is said to have "developed and maintained an inappropriately close and unprofessional relationship with [Sloan] while he exercised supervisory and operational authority over her protective detail that was inconsistent with federal impartiality and preferential-treatment standards."
      
    
            The report noted there isn't enough evidence to establish that Chavez-DeRemer and Sloan had a romantic or sexual relationship. However, the Inspector General did uncover hotel door lock records which “appeared to indicate” the two spent at least “portions overnight in the other’s room" during two trips to Las Vegas.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A witness also reported hearing Sloan use what they interpreted as a "sexual innuendo" while massaging Chavez-DeRemer's shoulders on one occasion. Chavez-DeRemer has been married to Shawn DeRemer since 1991.
      
    
            Chavez-DeRemer resigned as the Secretary of Labor in April ... after a little more than a year on the job.
      
    
            We've reached out to Lori ... so far, no word back.

            Perez Hilton apparently wanted to die at the hands of police, allegedly saying on his TikTok live stream that he was willing to hurt cops to make it happen -- according to documents obtained by TMZ.
      
    
            We've reviewed call logs detailing dispatch audio ... and one of the logs shows that the subject said on TikTok Live that he "wants to die by suicide by cops, and he will hurt police."
      
    
            We've also learned fire and rescue crews were initially told they could leave the area around 9:13 PM by cops ... but, nearly two hours later, cops asked them to return to the house and eventually entered the home with officers -- a strange development given Perez's serious need for medical attention.
      

            As we've told you ... Perez Hilton's sister called 911 during his mental health episode after finding him covered in blood with a strange look in his eyes. She immediately grabbed his children and fled the home. Dispatch audio we previously published captured the frantic rush to reach Perez.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            He was admitted to the hospital and treated for multiple injuries -- including several broken bones -- and an overdose. It seems he's still receiving mental health treatment at an inpatient facility.
